subject: botany
question_text: Mention the ploidy of any four of the following: (a) protonemal cell of a moss, (b) primary endosperm nucleus in a dicot, (c) leaf cell of a moss, (d) prothallus cell of a fern, (e) gemma cell in Marchantia, (f) meristem cell of a monocot, (g) ovum of a liverwort, (h) zygote of a fern.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack botany section, Chapter 4 Plant Kingdom, book p.7, VSAQ 11 — the NCERT in-text exercise. The book's scan garbles the list ('Protonema cell of mass', 'Leaf cell of a mass', 'Prothallus of a ferm', 'Zygote of ferm'); the question is restored to the NCERT wording (moss, fern, protonemal cell). The book's eight ploidy answers themselves are correct and are kept. This card answers all eight items because a student must know them all; the paper asks for any four. Only one source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card, not merely unrun. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Haploid (n) structures
lines: (a) Protonemal cell of a moss — n
(c) Leaf cell of a moss — n
(d) Prothallus cell of a fern — n
steps.why: Every structure that belongs to the gametophyte generation is haploid. The protonema, the moss leaf, the fern prothallus and the gemma are gametophyte parts, and the ovum is a gamete — so each is n.
common_mistakes: Marking the moss leaf 2n by treating it like an ordinary plant leaf — the leafy moss body is the gametophyte, so its leaf cell is n.
Marking the gemma 2n — a gemma is a vegetative bud of the gametophyte, so it is n.
steps.memory_tip: Ask one question for each item: which body made it? Gametophyte body → n; sporophyte body → 2n.
steps.margin_note: Write the letter and the ploidy symbol — no working is expected.

steps.label: Diploid (2n) and triploid (3n)
steps.why: The zygote and the whole plant body of a monocot belong to the sporophyte, so they are 2n. The primary endosperm nucleus forms by triple fusion — two polar nuclei plus one male gamete — so it is 3n.
common_mistakes: Writing 2n for the primary endosperm nucleus — triple fusion makes it 3n.
Writing n for the fern zygote — a zygote is always the fusion product, 2n.
steps.memory_tip: Only one 3n exists in the list — the endosperm nucleus, made of three fused nuclei.
steps.margin_note: Answer any four in the exam; the boxed rule line covers all eight.

insider_note: The paper asks for any four, but all eight items rotate across papers, so this card answers all eight — in the exam pick the four you are surest of.
